name: OCP coat (ABU cut) with blank name tape
size_basis: Outline traced from images/base/ABU_male.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, chosen so the coat is 29.96 in long. No real garment was measured. Sleeve cap and width were then modified by script for patch room, and the torso was widened x1.2 (estimate) so the purchase-description chest pocket fits. Length 29.96 in is about a Large Regular back length (30 in, GL/PD 14-04B Table VIIA; Medium Regular is 29-1/2); the Air Force wears this same Army OCP coat (DAFI 36-2903, which CAPR 39-1 7.1 points to) - that identity is an inference.

component_sources.note: Component sizes below are from the Army purchase description GL/PD 14-04B (rev B, Mar 2023; Detail Spec, Coat, Army Combat Uniform OCP), para 3.7 and Table VIIA, M/L/XL/XXL. Read by the coordination chat and relayed to this chat; rev B differs from rev A only in the upper sleeve pocket width (4-1/2 in, was 5). They are real inches in the coat's own coordinates only if the length scale is right.
not_drawn: cuff tab 2-1/8 x 3-1/8 (cuff tab rectangles removed on request)
left sleeve pencil pocket 2-3/8 wide, 2 channels (pen pockets removed on request; CAPR 39-1 7.1.1.1.2 makes it optional)
component_sources.chosen_size: Large Regular (back length 30 in); finished half chest 24-1/4 in is a flat measurement and is not comparable to the worn-view torso width drawn here

collar_slots.note: angle_deg: SVG rotate() convention (clockwise positive) to apply to an insignia whose long axis is vertical. cadet_* slots: cadet officer grade / cadet NCO metal chevron, centred 1 in from the collar FRONT edge, long axis parallel to it (cadet_axis = two points along that axis). officer_*: officer grade, centred 1 in from the collar BOTTOM edge, long axis perpendicular to it. size_in.along is measured along the long axis. bbox is the axis-aligned box of the rotated slot, also exposed as landmarks collar_*_zone_*. Right/left = wearer's.

landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box

chest_pocket.note: top edge rises toward the zipper; mirrored

beret_nbb_front.source: SHAPE TRACED on assets/refs/nbb/ethan-beret-shape-2026-10-29.png (Ethan's product photo of a navy beret, 301 x 300, from the wearer's left-front, the long point to the picture's left) by base-art/beret-nbb-measure-2.js, LIVE13-ART 4 (Ethan E88: "the beret should be 'longer' ... i like this shape better; less droopy"): the silhouette point by point (top edge y per x every 10 px, the right flank x per y, the band's straight bottom edge y 205 from x 107 to 269, the drape's lower edge, the point at x 11); the fold line (darkest column per row) and the crease above the band. Inch scale: the crown stands 125 px above the band in the photo = 3.282 in, the height the 2024 NBB group photo gave on real heads (beret-nbb-measure.js, 7.2 in head), so the band keeps its place on the head; the photo is oblique, its band's left end hidden under the drape, so the band width is not the scale and the point side is foreshortened (the drawn point is, if anything, short). Colour: the photo's dome #0d1321, lit flank #111c33; the dome brought to the former fill's luminance (x1.417) puts the lit flank at #182848; the fill moved a third of the way from #151932 toward it, #161e39 ("more blue (ever so slightly)"). CREST MEASURED on assets/refs/nbb/ethan-crest-photo-2026-10-29.png (Ethan's photo of the real pin, 467 x 473; E87 "st albans crest is wrong ... use this for the crest"): shield 355 px tall over 294 px greatest width (1.207), top edge 256 px (0.871 W) with rounded corners, sides bowing to the full width at 0.3 of the height and curving to one point (left side read, mirrored; degree-4 fit, rms 0.004 W), rim 4-7 px at the sides and 10-18 px at the lit top (drawn 0.03 W), saltire arms 0.19 W wide (perpendicular, mean of four runs) whose centre lines run from the top corners through the crossing 0.498 W below the top on the axis, field blue #3c4c92 (median); the rim and saltire read silver in the photo (#c7c0c0 lit, median #a6a2a2) but are drawn in the sheet's gold #f2d40a / #b8960a (the first NBB device's gold) at Ethan's word "the gold needs to be in the crest". Crest SIZE and HEIGHT on the beret from assets/refs/nbb/ethan-beret-crest-2026-10-29.png (Ethan's drawn beret, 250 x 167): crest 0.424 of the crown height tall (1.392 in), centre 0.496 of it above the band (1.628 in; the 2024 photo gave 1.625 in, kept), 1.693 in inboard of the band's wearer's-left corner (the 2024 photo's reading: the crest sits over the left eye, a place on the head). FOLD: the crease measured on the product photo is lifted (fold_over_crest.shift_in) so it passes 0.02 of the crest's height above the crest's top-left corner, Ethan: "the beret should be folded ... just over the first pixel in the top left corner of the crest"; his drawn beret's fold outline runs at the shield's top level (0.019 of its height below the top where it comes out at the shield's upper right). ESTIMATED: the headband strip height 0.315 in (12 px of the band's outer face at x 200 on the product photo). CAPR 39-1 6.2.3, ICL 25-02 9.2.3; LIVE13-ART 1, 4 and 5

edge_view.note: The shoulder pocket seen from the front (edge-on): the flat sleeve view narrowed to scale about the pocket centre line, turned by tilt_deg about the pivot (right: clockwise, left: counter-clockwise), its outer face on the sleeve edge. pivot_*_in are in sheet inches; visible_*: the silhouette near the pocket in the pocket frame as [v down from the pivot, u toward the centre line], 0.04 in inside it. Read by the engine instead of its own constants.
